# Continual-ARC instances

1. Read the current grid, demonstrations, remaining caps, and feedback. Infer a rule only when supported by examples. Before submitting, verify that the candidate reproduces every demo, including changed and unchanged cells.
2. For noisy grids with a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color, record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Test translations whose motif positions all contain zeros and recolor only those positions. Preserve the original motif and all other cells, including non-motif positions inside its bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation; test translations when the grid suggests a noisy background plus one seed object.
3. If full-width and full-height separator lines divide the grid into equal tiles and output dimensions match the tile layout, map each tile to one output cell. Use demos to identify the in-tile feature or count; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive. For the pattern with color-8 separators and 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, output 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise.
4. For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, check whether parallel lines have constant row−column (down-right) or row+column (down-left). If demos show a periodic color fill, use zero-based coordinates and index phases by column−row for down-right or row+column for down-left. Infer the smallest plausible period that does not assign different colors to the same residue; use demo outputs to establish the full phase-to-color mapping. Fill every cell by its phase, not just the sparse markers, and check cells on each demonstrated line. Do not infer unobserved residue colors from marker positions alone.
5. When color 1 marks an absent continuation at a grid edge, compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. It may be a solid suffix or selected motif-phase positions. Color only confirmed missing cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Choose repeated copies from demo evidence, not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
6. Use a small script to enumerate translations or construct outputs when manual scanning is error-prone. Account for seed shape and legal translations; allow rotation or reflection only when demos support it.
7. Choose exactly one legal action. Request a demonstration only when its expected information is worth its cost; submit when the rule is adequately supported; finish only after the instance is over. Account for scoring penalties and caps. Reply with only the action JSON object; do not call unrelated tools.
